title: Bandwidth-aware prioritized sync and store-and-forward data movement between edge applications and the NGC2/TAK data layer (policy-driven 'what leaves first, at what fidelity' and COP-edit reconciliation on reconnect)
problem: NGC2/TAK applications assume a coherent data layer, but tactical links are intermittent and thin (DARPA frames the regime as 1 Mbps down to 1 kbps), so edge nodes need a mission-policy-driven way to decide which data leaves first and at what fidelity, and how conflicting COP edits are reconciled on reconnection - today this is done by vendor-specific mesh/sync engines (Lattice Mesh, Ditto, TAK Server missions), per-application code and manual deconfliction.
echelons: expeditionary air base / contingency response element

user.exact_role: Primary: NGC2/TAK application developers and the data-layer integrator engineers who must make apps behave under DDIL; secondary: division/brigade G6/S6 and hub operators who decide which products get the link, and fires/intel/logistics cell users who reconcile duplicate or conflicting COP objects after partitions
user.echelon: Brigade and division (NGC2 hub-and-spoke), down to battalion/company nodes; Air Force expeditionary units for the AFLCMC/ACC variant
organization_examples: 4th Infantry Division (NGC2 prototype, Ivy Sting / Ivy Mass)
I Corps / III Armored Corps (early operational NGC2 fielding per press)
Team Anduril / Team Lockheed NGC2 integrators and their app vendors
AFLCMC Business and Enterprise Systems Directorate (Ditto sync buyer)
ACC contingency response / expeditionary comms units (AMIC Deployable Tactical Communications RFI)
TAK Product Center and TAK Server operators (ATAK/WinTAK missions)

current_workflow: Application writes to its local database / TAK client cache at the edge node (hub or spoke).
Link degrades or drops (jamming, terrain, movement, cloud loss); apps keep local state, some queue outbound updates, some silently drop them.
Operators keep fighting on the local picture; large products (imagery, FMV, mission packages) are pushed opportunistically, by hand, or not at all.

On reconnect, the sync engine (Lattice Mesh, Ditto CRDT sync, TAK Server mission change feed) replicates whatever it can, typically in arrival order rather than mission priority; large backlogs can saturate the thin link.
Operators and staff deconflict duplicate or conflicting tracks, graphics and edits by hand; some data is re-entered.
G6/S6 tune network QoS at the transport layer (radio priority, VLAN/QoS classes) because there is no application-level 'what leaves first' policy exposed to them.
current_solution: Inside NGC2: the Anduril-led common data layer baseline (Lattice + Palantir Foundry edge-to-cloud data mesh, Raft registries/federation) with hub-and-spoke edge nodes chosen specifically to cope with DDIL bandwidth/latency. Inside the TAK ecosystem: TAK Server missions / Data Sync plugin (clients subscribe and re-sync missed changes on reconnect; missions propagate across federation) plus commercial add-ons such as Ditto's Edge Sync plugin for ATAK. Air Force: Ditto cloud-to-edge sync platform (AFLCMC sole-source SBIR Phase II follow-on, $28M ceiling). Navy: DIU Common Operational Database prototypes (Ditto, Syntiant, HarperDB) for unmanned systems in DDIL. Collaboration: Immersive Wisdom 'ultra-low bandwidth' war rooms. Research: DARPA FLUID (2025) funding message re-encoding/suppression to cut C5ISRT transmission load under 1 Mbps-1 kbps. Workarounds: bespoke per-app queuing code, manual mission-package pushes, manual deconfliction.
failure: Two residual failures are evidenced or reasonably inferred: (1) prioritization is link-level or engine-default, not mission-phase policy ('send the fires target update before the imagery; downsample FMV; hold the logistics report') exposed to G6/S6 or the commander - DARPA had to launch FLUID in 2025 precisely because application/network messages are not yet intelligently reduced under DDIL (FACT that the program exists; INFERENCE that the gap is not closed operationally); (2) conflict-resolution semantics for C2 objects (tracks, graphics, orders edited on both sides of a partition) are engine-specific (CRDT last-writer-wins style in Ditto, opaque in Lattice/Foundry, mission change-log in TAK Server) and not auditable by operators, so duplicates/conflicts are reconciled by hand (INFERENCE from segment agents; no public government document quantifies this). The store-and-forward / re-sync primitive itself is NOT unsolved: Ivy Mass (May 2026) publicly demonstrated local tracking and later synchronization after losing the division cloud.

evidence.claim: AFLCMC (Business and Enterprise Systems Directorate) awarded DittoLive a ceiling $28,000,000 sole-source FFP contract (SBIR Phase II extension) for the full Ditto cloud-to-edge sync platform, with $4,188,712 FY25 RDT&E and $1,097,000 FY25 O&M obligated at award; work through July 10, 2028. Ceiling is not revenue; only ~$5.3M obligated at award.
evidence.source_title: DoD Contracts for July 11, 2025 (GlobalSecurity mirror of DoD announcement)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DARPA's FLUID program (posted March 28, 2025; abstracts due April 21, 2025) seeks software that intercepts, reasons over and manipulates control-plane and data-plane messages to reduce C5ISRT transmission load under DDIL network capacities from 1 Mbps down to 1 kbps without losing application utility - i.e., the government treats application-aware load reduction as an open research problem.
evidence.source_title: FLUID: Flexible Networking Using Intelligent Dialecting (DARPA program page; special notice DARPA-SN-25-66)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Ivy Mass (May 2026) tested NGC2 at division scale under simulated cyberattack, EMI and degraded communications; units continued tracking the battle locally after losing division-cloud access and synchronized once connectivity returned - proving the requirement and that a baseline store-and-forward/re-sync capability already exists inside the prime's stack.
evidence.source_title: Ivy Mass exercises NGC2 at division scale (army.mil)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DIU's Common Operational Database project with Project Overmatch and NIWC Pacific awarded prototype agreements to Ditto, Syntiant and HarperDB for databases that let unmanned systems operate in DDIL; DIU reported all three met project goals and that the Navy was awarding success memos and moving toward production contracts - prototype success, not evidenced production scale.
evidence.source_title: Defense Innovation Unit Announces Results of Maritime AI Project (ExecutiveGov)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: TAK Server already stores mission data server-side; clients subscribe to a mission to receive dynamic updates or to synchronize data missed while disconnected, and missions propagate across federation boundaries - the reconnect re-sync primitive exists in the government-owned TAK baseline, but there is no mission-priority or fidelity policy in that mechanism.
evidence.source_title: Mission API / Data Sync - OpenTAKServer documentation (mirrors TAK Server Mission API behaviour)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Anduril markets Lattice Mesh as a decentralized mesh that bi-directionally transports data in DDIL environments; CDAO awarded Anduril a three-year production agreement to scale a tactical Edge Data Mesh (Dec 2024) and opened it to third-party developers - vendor marketing is not proof the prioritization/reconciliation problem is solved, but it is proof the incumbent owns the interface.
evidence.source_title: Decentralizing battle data: CDAO, Anduril open tactical 'mesh' to third-party developers (Breaking Defense)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Army established the NGC2 common data layer baseline (June 2026) with Anduril lead; Lattice + Palantir Foundry provide the edge-to-cloud data mesh and Raft the registries/transformation/federation - the sync/prioritization function sits inside a prime-owned layer, so an outside vendor must integrate through the prime.
evidence.source_title: Army and industry align on common data baseline, as NGC2 moves from prototyping to delivery (army.mil)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Hub-and-spoke NGC2 architecture was chosen specifically to address bandwidth and latency in DDIL, and 4ID reported it 'drastically eliminated lag time' after PC-C5 lessons - implying material latency/bandwidth problems in the prior iteration.
evidence.source_title: Army's 4th Infantry Division kicks off Ivy Sting exercises to scale NGC2 prototype (Federal News Network)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: ACC AMIC 'Deployable Tactical Communications' RFI asks for routing, edge compute, application-level QoS and cross-domain data sharing for expeditionary operations in contested forward environments (responses due Feb 25, 2026) - an Air Force ask for application-level prioritization, though as part of a comms kit, not a standalone software line.
evidence.source_title: ACC AMIC Deployable Tactical Communications RFI (sam.gov; primary page blocked this session, from earlier stage E02-F24)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: It largely has been solved at the primitive level and by well-funded players: Ditto (~$136M raised; AFLCMC $28M-ceiling sole-source; DIU COD success memo; ATAK Edge Sync plugin) sells exactly 'sync that survives intermittent links'; Anduril's Lattice Mesh has a CDAO production agreement and now leads the NGC2 data layer with Palantir Foundry; TAK Server's Mission API re-syncs missed changes for free in government-owned software. What remains - mission-phase policy for ordering/fidelity and auditable C2-object conflict resolution - is a thin layer that lives inside those engines' APIs, and the engines' owners (Anduril/Palantir for NGC2, Ditto for the Air Force, TAK Product Center for TAK) control the interface. A standalone startup would be selling a policy layer to the very companies that would rather build it, with no independent government buyer evidenced for 'prioritization policy' as a product; DARPA FLUID (2025) shows the government is instead funding this as research through performers.
technical_wedge: If pursued at all: an engine-agnostic 'mission data QoS' sidecar/SDK that (a) scores every outbound object by mission phase, echelon, object type and age against live link telemetry (MANET/LEO throughput, loss, latency) and emits an ordered, fidelity-degraded queue (track deltas before imagery; tiled/downsampled imagery; FMV keyframes only), (b) exposes explicit, auditable merge rules per C2 object type (track, graphic, order, mission-package) with a reconcile log operators can review, and (c) plugs into TAK Server missions, Ditto's SDK or Lattice/Foundry APIs rather than replacing them. The defensible IP is the policy language plus measured link models, not the sync engine. Alternative, narrower wedge with clearer buyer: a DDIL network-emulation and sync-behaviour test harness (the Army's own SBIR/xTech ask) that scores any vendor stack on 'what arrived first and at what fidelity' - a tooling business, not a data-layer business.

mvp.what: Open-source-friendly sidecar + policy DSL that sits between an ATAK/WinTAK-CIV client or a sample logistics/fires app and TAK Server (and optionally Ditto SDK), with a netem/Linux tc link shaper reproducing 1 Mbps to 1 kbps, 30-minute partitions and reconnect storms across ~10 simulated nodes.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Side-by-side demo: naive TAK/Ditto replication vs. policy-driven replication over identical shaped links, showing time-to-arrival of priority objects (e.g., fires target updates, medevac requests) cut by a measured factor, zero duplicate tracks after partition, and an operator-readable reconcile log; run on commercial laptops/SBCs and Wi-Fi/LTE plus a throttled Starlink or a pair of commercial mesh radios.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That mission-policy ordering and fidelity degradation deliver a measurable operational benefit (priority objects arrive first, link not saturated on reconnect) that the incumbent engine defaults do not, AND that an integrator or the TAK Product Center is willing to consume it via an API - the second is the real test.

data_requirement.what: Cursor-on-Target/TAK object schemas and mission-package formats; representative message mixes per mission phase (volume, size, object types); tactical link telemetry traces (MANET/LEO throughput, loss, latency over time); later, exercise data on partition events and reconciliation actions (likely CUI).
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: CoT schemas, ATAK-CIV and TAK Server docs are public (ATAK-CIV/SDK open-sourced on GitHub; TAK-GOV/MIL distribution-controlled). Message mixes and link traces can be synthesized or measured on commercial mesh radios/Starlink. Real exercise partition data requires being inside an NGC2 team or a CRADA with C5ISR Center - not obtainable as an outsider, and CUI/ITAR questions need counsel if a non-US-person founder touches it.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily. Anduril/Palantir own the NGC2 data mesh and its APIs, already sell 'DDIL-optimized' as a headline feature, and hold a CDAO production agreement; Ditto's engine is the natural place to add mission-priority queues and merge policies; TAK Product Center can extend the Mission API. Adding a policy scheduler and merge-rule engine is weeks-to-months of work for teams that already own the sync loop and the link telemetry.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Reject as a standalone company. The only credible startup positions are (a) a plugin/tooling vendor inside the TAK ecosystem or an NGC2 team, or (b) an acqui-hire target for Ditto/Raft/Anduril after proving a measurably better prioritization/merge layer. Neither supports venture-scale independence; the 'policy above vendor meshes' idea has no evidenced independent buyer, and the government is funding the research path through DARPA FLUID instead.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The MVP is unclassified, uses open TAK-CIV software and commercial radios. Beyond MVP: TAK-GOV/MIL are distribution-controlled; NGC2 exercise data and link performance data are typically CUI; deploying inside a prime's environment requires ATO inheritance and possibly cleared staff; radio integrations may touch ITAR-controlled technical data. Sale of the software itself is likely EAR territory but this needs counsel - no legal determination made.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: SBIR/STTR >50% U.S.-citizen/permanent-resident ownership and control rule means the Indonesian founder cannot be part of the qualifying majority; access to CUI/ITAR technical data by a non-U.S. person may require an export license or exclusion from that work (deemed-export rules); a FOCI mitigation may be needed for any facility clearance. Requires export-control and immigration counsel; the German founder's path to permanent residency changes but does not remove these questions.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Bandwidth-aware prioritized sync has real commercial analogues (Ditto's commercial base in aviation, retail and maritime; IoT fleets; disaster response with TAK-CIV users such as CBP, FEMA, wildland fire). But the specific mission-phase policy and C2-object merge semantics are military; commercial buyers want generic sync, which Ditto and open-source local-first stacks already supply.

defensibility.explanation: Possible moat: a validated library of mission-phase priority policies and measured link models, plus reconcile-rule sets per C2 object type, and the exercise-derived data to tune them. Weak in practice because the engine owners see all the same data, control the APIs and can replicate a scheduler; no network effects or accreditation moat accrue to a sidecar.

why_now: NGC2 moved from prototypes to a common data-layer baseline (Jun 2026) with division-scale exercises (Ivy Mass May 2026, Lightning Surge Mar 2026) that create measurable partition events; Anduril opened Lattice Mesh to third-party developers (Dec 2024); DARPA launched FLUID (Mar 2025) explicitly for application-aware load reduction under 1 Mbps-1 kbps; the Air Force converted Ditto's SBIR into a $28M-ceiling sole-source platform buy (Jul 2025); commercial pLEO and MANET transport are proliferating, so the mismatch between app assumptions and thin links is now visible at scale rather than hypothetical.
killer_risk: Feature, not product. The store-and-forward/re-sync primitive already works inside Lattice/Foundry, Ditto and TAK Server (Ivy Mass demonstrated it), the residual policy/merge layer is a modest extension for the engine owners, the government funds the research path through DARPA FLUID performers rather than buying a product, and no independent buyer for a 'prioritization policy layer' is evidenced anywhere in public procurement - so the startup either becomes a plugin shop dependent on a prime or is acqui-hired at a small multiple.

allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling with allies, but not enough to change the verdict. TAK is used widely by NATO and partner forces, so a TAK plugin has a natural allied channel; Germany's D-LBO/TaWAN LBO (Rheinmetall, blackned) and the UK's Project Asgard (where Anduril UK demonstrated an edge data mesh) face the same DDIL sync problem without an Anduril/Palantir-owned data layer yet, and a German founder could credibly sell into the Bundeswehr ecosystem. However, allied programs also have their own incumbents (blackned, Systematic SitaWare, Thales) and the U.S. export-control posture of a U.S.-based product complicates the allied route; the more realistic allied play is a policy/sync layer built on TAK for NATO users, which is a niche service business.
